summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease with multiple prior stents, hypertension, and dyslipidemia was admitted for evaluation of sudden-onset chest pain at rest, which resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin. He also reported labile blood pressure and orthostatic hypotension. Initial ECG and serial troponins were normal, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. A chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities. He underwent an exercise stress MIBI test, which revealed ischemic ECG changes during exertion but normal myocardial perfusion and a preserved ejection fraction of 52%. The known 70% stenosis in the PDA was deemed unsuitable for intervention. He was treated with IV fluids for mild dehydration related to his mitochondrial myopathy, with improvement in creatinine from 1.4 to 1.2 mg/dL. Blood pressure management was optimized by switching from oral clonidine to a weekly patch and increasing isosorbide mononitrate to 30 mg daily. He remained in normal sinus rhythm, with no arrhythmic events. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and instructions to follow up with cardiology.
